exactAttacks.relevance: Defines the reviewed fixed-length mode as Trunc_d(P(x)+x); feed-forward is crucial to its ideal-permutation one-wayness argument. The M_C=I equivalence assumes unconstrained input.

Corrects the original subspace-trail/Groebner model. Compression is modeled with c=0; feed-forward changes equations but not their number or degree. No full recommended instance is reported broken. Conjecture 1 remains unproved and experiments can be non-regular.

Uses operation-mode constraints and the P_{t/4} tensor M4 external structure. H1 t=16,d=7 has a two-round skip [1]^1+[7]^3+[49]^3. H3 t=24,d=10 has [1]^2+[7]^2+[49]^6. H4 t=24,d=11 has [1]^1+[7]^3+[49]^7.

Compression/sponge attacks can outperform CICO analysis. Its greater-than-2^100 statement is a speedup over prior algebraic complexity, not a 106-bit attack and not a break. Its full-round conclusion depends on a quadratic ideal-degree lower bound and tightness assumptions.

Proposed mitigations are more external rounds, an MDS external layer, or swapped M4 tensor P_{t/4}. None may be adopted silently: each defines a new exact permutation and constants/vector/review packet.
